concerns_addressed: PRE-EXISTING FAILURES (out of scope, NOT attributed to T8): `php artisan test --filter=OrderTest` at HEAD 29b0fc2 gives 2 failed / 34 passed. The 2 failures are exactly `cannot approve already confirmed order` (OrderTest.php:314) and `concurrent admin approvals append one confirmed history` (OrderTest.php:626) â€” both assert 422 on idempotent re-approve while the codebase now returns 200. Verified the T8 diff touches NEITHER those tests NOR approve/cancel logic (git diff shows 0 matches for those test names; approve/show/cancel/runApprovalTransaction/approveInTransaction/approvalResponse are byte-identical to parent 421996b). The 6 new T8 tests pass (6 passed, 33 assertions) and the other 28 pre-existing tests pass.
Admin guard unchanged: `if (! $request->user()->isAdmin()) { ... 403 }` is byte-identical to parent 421996b (OrderController.php:71-76).
`formatOrderResponse()` byte-identical to parent (verified via diff of the method body) â€” `data` item keys unchanged.

`?cursor=<n>` returns the SECOND page by OFFSET, not id-based: test 2 creates OLDEST=id1(Jan), NEWEST=id2(Mar), MIDDLE=id3(Feb); created_at DESC â†’ page1=NEWEST, page2=MIDDLE at cursor=1. An id-based cursor would return NEWEST first, so the assertion is genuinely offset-semantic.

Nulls-last claim is observable, not just asserted: orders.created_at is nullable (Laravel `timestamps()` â†’ `nullable()`), and I executed the generated expression `(created_at IS NULL) ASC, created_at DESC, id DESC` in SQLite â€” a NULL row sorts LAST on both ASC and DESC. The `id DESC` tiebreak is deterministic.

index() is 51 lines (OrderController.php:69-119) vs the ~50-line budget â€” within the approximate tolerance; the two new private helpers (scalarQueryString, buildListMeta) were extracted to keep it small.

Spec text says `->offset()` before `->limit()`; implementation chains `->limit($limit + 1)` then `->offset($cursor)`. Functionally identical in Eloquent: limit/offset set independent builder properties and the grammar always compiles `LIMIT x OFFSET y` regardless of call order. No behavioural difference (all page tests green).

strengths: Additive-only diff confined to the 2 in-scope files; ListQuery helper (App\Support\ListQuery) already existed at parent 421996b and was reused, not modified.

Sort allowlist is enforced via ListQuery::resolveSort + orderByRaw(ListQuery::rawOrder(...)); the only orderBy in the file is the resolved allowlist column (OrderController.php:105) â€” no column name is ever interpolated from raw user input, and `?sort=evil; DROP TABLE orders--` returns 200.

Scalar-safe reads verified end-to-end: `limit[]=5`, `cursor[]=x&sort[]=y&order[]=z`, `sort[]=x`, `sort=__proto__`, `sort=created_at&order=BOGUS`, `limit=abc`, `cursor=-3` all return HTTP 200 (no 500 / Array-to-string).
meta.total derives from an unfiltered clone taken BEFORE order/limit/offset (OrderController.php:98-101, 104-108) â€” the test with limit=1 proves total stays the full count (3), not the page length.
Response shape exactly matches spec: {status, data, meta:{has_more, limit, cursor, total}}; `data` items still produced by the untouched formatOrderResponse.

Tests are non-vacuous: sort-by-status test is constructed so default created_at DESC yields the OPPOSITE order from status ASC (comment documents this), so it only passes when ?sort is honoured; fallback/array tests assert both 200 and the default newest-first order.
Clear explanatory comments at each decision point (allowlist fallback, total-from-unfiltered-clone, limit+1 technique).

issues.description: OrderController.php is now 314 lines (was 255 pre-T8), marginally above the ~300-line refactor heuristic. Downgraded to Minor (not Important) because: the threshold is approximate ('~300'), the excess is ~5%, index() itself is within its ~50-line budget, growth is a small cohesive additive change (2 focused helpers), and the task was explicitly additive-only forbidding broader restructuring. Flagging for future tasks that touch this controller.

Redundant double clone: buildListMeta() receives an already-cloned builder and clones it again (`(clone $query)->count()`), while the call site also passes `clone $query`. Harmless (count() does not mutate the builder) but the inner clone is superfluous.
